chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah who said:

I asked him about the visitation of the graves and the construction of the mosques therein, so he said: As for the visitation to the graves, there is no problem with it, and do not build the mosques by them.

key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ بِهَا: There is no problem with it / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on building mosques at the site of graves in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Sama’ah ibn Mi’ran reports to Imam al-Sadiq that while visiting graves is permissible, building mosques directly at the grave sites is discouraged. This ruling reflects the Shia emphasis on distinguishing between honoring the deceased through visitation and avoiding the potential for shirk or innovation (bid'ah) associated with treating graves as places of worship, a key theme in the purification of monotheism.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about visitation of the graves and construction of the Masjids therein, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘As for the visitation to the graves, so there is no problem, but do not build the Masjids by these’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah who has said the following: “
I asked (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about visiting graves and building Masjids there. He said, ‘There is no offense in visiting graves, but Masjid must not be built there.’”
